{"jobs":[{"id":"83ce7ac0-159a-4fa7-8145-0848affe3d0a","title":"Associate Video Producer","department":"Media","team":"Media","employmentType":"FullTime","location":"San Francisco","secondaryLocations":[],"publishedAt":"2026-10-14T19:35:51.556+00:00","isListed":true,"isRemote":null,"workplaceType":null,"address":{"postalAddress":{"addressRegion":"California","addressCountry":"USA","addressLocality":"San Francisco"}},"jobUrl":"https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ycombinator/83ce7ac0-159a-4fa7-8145-0848affe3d0a","applyUrl":"https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ycombinator/83ce7ac0-159a-4fa7-8145-0848affe3d0a/application","descriptionHtml":"

Y Combinator is the leading startup accelerator for entrepreneurs. Since 2005, YC has invested in over 6,000 companies, including Airbnb, Dropbox, OpenAI, Stripe, Reddit, DoorDash, Coinbase, and Instacart. Today, YC has built the most powerful startup community in the world and is committed to supporting founders for the life of their company.

Job Description:

Y Combinator is looking for an Associate Video Producer to join the YC Media team. This is a role for someone who is smart, organized, resourceful, and already immersed in startups and technology. You’ll work closely with our Senior Video Producers across videos, podcasts, interviews, and other editorial projects. You’ll help with everything from research and pre-interviews to editing, publishing, scheduling, guest communication, and keeping our production calendar on track.

A lot of this job is making sure things actually get finished. You should be the kind of person who notices what needs to happen next, follows up without being asked, and is happy moving between creative work and the less glamorous details that keep a production running smoothly.

Just as importantly, you should understand the world YC operates in. You follow startups, AI, technology, and the people building them. You know what people in this world are talking about, can quickly understand why something matters, and have enough context to ask good questions rather than starting from zero every time.

What you'll do:

Help produce YC videos and podcasts

  • Work with Senior Video Producers to move projects from idea to shoot to final publication.

  • Research guests, companies, technologies, and topics.

  • Help write interview questions, briefs, descriptions, and other editorial material.

  • Schedule and conduct pre-interviews, take detailed notes, and report back to producers.

  • Coordinate shoot dates and logistics with founders, companies, and guests.

  • Review edits and help prepare projects for final approval.

  • Edit short-form clips and other video content.

Keep productions organized

  • Maintain notes and project documentation throughout the production process.

  • Keep project cards, production schedules, shoot calendars, and publishing calendars up to date.

  • Track where every project is in the pipeline and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.

  • Manage transcripts, video files, review links, and other production assets.

  • Download and organize final videos and other assets in Dropbox.

  • Transcribe finished recordings.

  • Send final edits, transcripts, file links, and YouTube links to YC partners and other collaborators.

Help publish and distribute our work

  • Upload and publish episodes across YouTube, podcast platforms, and other channels.

  • Make sure titles, descriptions, thumbnails, transcripts, chapters, and other publishing assets are ready.

  • Help coordinate the final steps between editorial, production, and distribution.

Help things run smoothly on shoot days

  • Welcome guests and help get them where they need to be.

  • Make sure guests have water, food, and anything else they need.

  • Help keep sets clean, reset, and ready for the next shoot.

  • Occasionally assist as a camera operator.

  • Help keep our production gear and equipment organized.

You might be a good fit if:

  • You’re deeply interested in startups, AI, technology, and the internet, and already understand YC and startup culture. You know the companies, people, ideas, and conversations that matter in this world.

  • You’re intellectually curious and learn quickly. You can get up to speed on an unfamiliar company or technical subject without needing everything explained to you.

  • You have some experience producing or editing video, podcasts, or other media.

  • You’re a strong writer and researcher with good editorial instincts. You can recognize what’s actually interesting about a person, company, or idea and explain complicated technical topics clearly.

  • You’re extremely organized, reliable, and comfortable managing lots of small details across several projects at once. You communicate clearly and follow up quickly.

  • You’re willing to do whatever needs to be done to make a production successful, whether that’s editing a clip, researching a guest, updating a calendar, or grabbing lunch for a shoot.

  • You have strong attention to detail. A wrong link, missing file, forgotten follow-up, or stale calendar entry bothers you. You should be able to spot the difference between Arial and Helvetica or know if it's a Dutch or French flag.

  • You have some hands-on experience with cameras, audio, and video production equipment. You don’t need to be an expert, but you should be comfortable helping set up and operate gear on shoots.

  • You’re able to safely lift up to 50 pounds as needed for production gear and shoot setup.

  • This is a good role for someone early in their media career who wants to learn the entire production process rather than specialize in one narrow part of it.

  • You might currently be an assistant producer, production assistant, video editor, podcast producer, editorial assistant, or someone who has been making your own projects and wants to do this professionally. We're less interested in a particular resume than whether you're sharp, curious, capable, and genuinely plugged into the world we cover.

  • The best person for this role will be equally comfortable thinking about what makes a piece of content good and doing the hundred small things required to actually get it published.

Location: YC is headquartered in San Francisco, and candidates must reside in the San Francisco Bay Area. Our Media Team works from our Dogpatch offices in San Francisco at least three days per week, with additional in-office days as filming schedules require. Some projects may also require travel and weekend work.

 

Compensation: $180,000-$200,000 salary (depending on skills and experience).

 

Benefits: Our full benefits package includes medical, vision, and dental plans, an infertility benefit, STD/LTD, life insurance, commuter benefits, a flexible spending account, a health savings account, a 401(k) with 4% matching, generous parental leave, paid holidays, and a flexible paid time off policy.

 

Work Authorization: This position does not support work authorization/visa sponsorship.

 

Y Combinator considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law, including San Francisco’s Fair Chance Ordinance. Y Combinator is committed to protecting the privacy of job applicants' personal information and to complying with the California Consumer Privacy Act. The privacy policy of Ashby, Inc., the hiring platform used by Y Combinator, governs the collection of such data and is available here.

Y Combinator is the leading startup accelerator for entrepreneurs. Since 2005, YC has invested in over 6,000 companies, including Airbnb, Dropbox, OpenAI, Stripe, Reddit, DoorDash, Coinbase, and Instacart. Today, YC has built the most powerful startup community in the world and is committed to supporting founders for the life of their company.

Job Description:

Y Combinator is looking for an Editorial Researcher to join the YC Media team. We make content for people who are curious about startups, technology, AI, science, and the future. That includes videos and podcasts, essays, original research, and new projects built around the enormous amount of knowledge and data that exists inside YC.

We're looking for someone who is unusually curious, technically inclined, and a very good writer. You should be able to understand a complicated idea, figure out what's actually interesting about it, and explain it simply without dumbing it down.

This isn't a traditional writing or editing job. You'll research stories, analyze data, develop ideas with YC partners and founders, help shape videos and podcasts, write and edit articles, and experiment with new kinds of editorial projects.

What you'll do:

  • Research, write, and edit YC’s written content.

  • Develop ideas and do research for YC videos, podcasts, interviews, and other media.

  • Work directly with YC partners, founders, and the rest of the Media team to turn interesting ideas into great content.

  • Dig into data to find surprising trends about startups, technology, founders, and what people are building.

  • Find interesting people, projects, papers, companies, and ideas before everyone else is talking about them.

  • Help us figure out what YC should be covering and why.

  • Take complicated technical subjects and make them clear, accurate, and interesting.

  • Experiment with new editorial formats and ways of telling stories.

You might be a good fit if:

  • You're deeply curious about technology and understand the culture around startups, AI, engineering, and the internet.

  • You're an excellent writer and editor. You can make complicated things simple without making them simplistic.

  • You're technical enough to talk to engineers and researchers and understand what they're actually saying.

  • You like going down rabbit holes, reading papers, digging through datasets, talking to experts, and figuring things out for yourself.

  • You have strong editorial judgment. You can recognize when something is genuinely interesting rather than merely popular.

  • You're comfortable working across formats. An idea might become a Substack post, a YouTube video, a podcast conversation, a chart, or something we haven't tried yet.

  • You're opinionated about media and the internet and have good instincts about what smart people actually want to read and watch.

  • You don't need someone to hand you a story. You find them.

There isn't one obvious background for this role. You might be an engineer who loves writing, someone from developer relations, a technical journalist, a data journalist, a researcher, a former founder, or someone who has worked at a think tank. We're much more interested in how you think, how you write, and what you've made than what your previous title was.

Above all, we're looking for someone who is smart, curious, technically adventurous, and wants to make things that smart people genuinely want to read and watch.

Location: YC is headquartered in San Francisco, and candidates must reside in the San Francisco Bay Area. Our Media Team works from our Dogpatch offices in San Francisco at least three days per week, with additional in-office days as filming schedules require. Some projects may also require travel and weekend work.

 

Compensation: $180,000-$200,000 salary (depending on skills and experience).

 

Benefits: Our full benefits package includes medical, vision, and dental plans, an infertility benefit, STD/LTD, life insurance, commuter benefits, a flexible spending account, a health savings account, a 401(k) with 4% matching, generous parental leave, paid holidays, and a flexible paid time off policy.

Y Combinator is hiring a Director of Early Access to help YC founders win customers and help established companies discover and adopt new AI products.

About the Early Access Network

The Early Access Network is YC's invite-only network for senior leaders who can evaluate and deploy AI at their companies. It connects buyers with YC founders through events and digital channels. Buyers get direct access to new products from YC founders. Founders get real feedback and relationships with potential customers.

Since launching in October, the Network already includes hundreds of leaders from the world’s top companies. We want to grow the program across YC batch and alumni companies and build a digital version so these connections can happen year-round.

The role

You'll run Early Access day-to-day, with primary responsibility for building and managing relationships with buyers at Fortune 500 companies and leading YC companies. You'll work closely with YC Partners as well as our engineering and events teams to grow the program.

You'll personally own important relationships and use agents to expand what you can accomplish without building a large team. You should be as comfortable following up with a YC founder in the current batch as leading a conversation with a senior public company executive. The role reports to the YC Partner responsible for managing all of Early Access.

What you'll do

  • Grow and manage the Network. Find and qualify new members, understand their priorities, and build relationships.

  • Connect buyers with relevant YC companies. Work with YC Partners and founders to understand their products, identify good matches, and help founders prepare for conversations and follow up effectively.

  • Oversee events for batch and alumni companies. Work with YC Events teammates on planning and execution, with particular attention to who is in the room and follow-ups.

  • Continue to build the digital version of Early Access with YC Partners and YC's engineering team. Turn buyer and founder needs into product priorities.

  • Measure KPIs and improve the program. Track relevant introductions, pilots, paid customer relationships, and repeat buyer participation. Learn where opportunities stall and help address the causes.

What we're looking for

  • At least 10 years of experience owning critical customer or partner relationships in technology, with exceptional results.

  • You've operated in a venture-backed startup and understand how large companies work.

  • You understand how companies evaluate, buy, and deploy AI, including the people and processes involved in getting a pilot into prod.

  • You can earn the trust of founders, senior executives, and YC Partners

  • You're organized, comfortable with numbers, and reliable about complex follow-through. You can turn an open-ended goal into a working program, without a large staff or layers of process.

  • You can understand what users need, make sensible tradeoffs, and work closely with engineers to build something people want.

  • You’re excited about managing a team of agents vs. a large team of people.

  • Genuine belief in YC's mission of helping founders build generational companies. You're excited to continue to build Early Access. This is an operating role, not an investing position.

Location

YC is headquartered in the SF Bay Area. Candidates must live in the SF Bay Area or be willing to relocate. Some travel may be required.

Compensation

Base salary range: $325,000-$400,000 plus performance bonuses.

Benefits

Our full benefits package includes medical, vision, and dental plans, an infertility benefit, STD/LTD, life insurance, commuter benefits, a flexible spending account, a health savings account, a 401(k) with 4% matching, generous parental leave, paid holidays, and a flexible paid time off policy.

Work authorization

This position does not support work authorization/visa sponsorship.

Fair chance and applicant privacy

Y Combinator considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law, including San Francisco’s Fair Chance Ordinance.

Y Combinator is committed to protecting the privacy of job applicants' personal information and to complying with the California Consumer Privacy Act. The privacy policy of Ashby, Inc., the hiring platform used by Y Combinator, governs the collection of such data and is available here.

About Y Combinator

Y Combinator was created by startup founders to provide the support they wished they had when building and growing their own companies. Since 2005, YC has funded and supported more than 6,000 startups with a combined valuation of over $2 trillion. These include Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, Coinbase, Reddit, Instacart, OpenAI, Dropbox, Twitch, Brex, Ginkgo Bioworks, Scale AI, Deel, Webflow, GitLab, Flexport, Segment, Rippling, Helion Energy, and Zapier. The YC alumni network is widely regarded as one of the world's most influential entrepreneurial communities, connecting thousands of founders and technology leaders across every major sector of innovation.
